I investigated the compiler pipeline and traced the memoization loss back to reactive scope construction and mutable-range analysis.

The callback itself isn't special, and the memoization drop occurs after `FlattenScopesWithHooksOrUseHIR` prunes a scope that spans `getIsChromatic()`, `useResizeDetector()`, the callback, and the `classnames(..., { isChromatic })` path.

The interesting part is that `getIsChromatic()` is treated as `ValueKind.Mutable` because it has no known function signature. That causes alias propagation and mutable-range expansion through the object literal passed to `classnames`, which eventually places the callback and classnames path into the same reactive scope.

The resulting scope crosses the hook boundary and is pruned, which removes callback memoization.

I also found existing compiler tests and comments describing similar mutable-range entanglement cases as a known limitation, including a fixture comment stating:

> "This function should be memoized, but its mutable range is entangled with the useContext call..."

So before attempting a fix, it may be useful to clarify whether #36800 is expected behavior under the current mutability model, or whether the scope construction here is considered overly conservative compared to the intended optimization goals.
